name: Feng Chia University (SUSPENDED)
overview:
Additional Programme Specifics

  • Not recommended for students with a Chinese passport


Feng Chia University

Feng Chia University was founded in 1961 and it is located 100 Wenhwa Road, Seatwen in the city of Taichung. Nearly 18 000 students go there. It is ranked in the top best universities in Asia by the Times Higher Education Supplement (2013).

Taichung is a municipality in central Taiwan. It is Taiwan's second-largest city, with more than 2.86 million residents.
administrative:
1. Application dossier

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application. Your host university may ask for the following documents:

  • Filled out application form with your photo above.
  • Transcripts in English (transcripts will be provided by IAFF).
  • Study plan in English (Indicate the courses you have chosen and your motivation for attending this university as well as your objectives after this year of study).
  • 2 letters of recommendation (teacher, internship tutor).
  • Copy of passport (non-Taiwanese passport).
  • Tepitech score certificate downloadable from the intra.

To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract.
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier.

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.

2. Visa

Once you’ve submitted your application, FCU will review your documents and will issue an Acceptance Letter.

Students have mentioned it takes about a month.

Once you arrive in Taiwan, within 30 days, you must obtain a residence permit (ARC). You must provide the university with your proof of residence permit.

Please note:

  • If you hold a Chinese nationality, you will have to obtain and complete an additional document ‘Entry and Exit Permit Taiwan Republic of China’. This document will be sent to you by FCU.
  • As you are staying a full year at FCU, you must apply for Resident Visa at the Taipei representative office in France: http://www.roc-taiwan.org/fr_fr/post/8905.html
  • You must also complete the Health Report (Form B), that FCU will send you.
  • For your visa application, you will be asked to provide proof of financial resources (personal resources of at least 600 euros per month).

3. Insurance and Health

You must subscribe to the insurance provided by Feng Chia University according to the regulations for welcoming international students in Taiwan.

All international students are asked to complete a medical exam upon arrival in Taiwan. This includes in particular:

  • a chest X-ray for tuberculosis
  • a measles test
  • a rubella test

If you have been vaccinated against these last two diseases, you will need to provide a certificate of vaccination. For this exam, you will have to pay the sum of NT $750, or about 20 euros.

We also highly recommend you to purchase an international insurance in France that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.

To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

After holding ARCs for over six months, students are obliged to carry National Health Insurance (NHI). Fee: about about NT$749/month (20€).

For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/taiwan

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.

4. Prepare your arrival

For advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on Taiwan, click here.

To familiarize yourself with the city of Taichung, please consult the information below:

  • http://en.fcu.edu.tw/wSite/lp?ctNode=45175&mp=3&idPath=19354_45172_45175
  • http://eng.taichung.gov.tw/mp.aspx?mp=49

5. Campus life

Every exchange student will be assigned 1–2 volunteer students. Our buddy group will help with airport pick-up, registration, and course selection. Airport pick-up service requires an extra fee.

Utilities fees are mandatory to pay for each semester (around 40 euros).
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation

FCU has on-campus accommodation but the dorms are not available for exchange students.


Off-campus accommodation

It is difficult to generalize because comfort and location criteria vary and affect rent prices but monthly rent for a room in a shared apartment can go between 7000NT to 8500NT (200-250€), plus a deposit fee of two months' rent. Make sure to ask for a contract in English. When you sign the lease, in addition to the first month's rent, the landlord will generally ask for two months' rent as a deposit. The deposit will be returned in full or deducted based on the condition of the accommodation at the time of departure. As photos are not always reliable, we suggest you not to sign a long-term lease before you arrive in Taiwan and inspect the accommodation in person. You can book an AirBnb or a hotel room two weeks before school to visit studios.

You can refer to this link for housing information in Taichung.

  1. Private room in an apartment with roommates

There are active Facebook groups. You should start looking during the summer (about 1 month/1 month and a half before back to school in September).

  1. Private accommodation

You can choose to live in an apartment of your own. Please note that in this case you probably won't have a kitchen in your studio. Some websites include Myroomabroad (English) or 591 (Chinese).
courses:
Credits

You will need to obtain 30 local credits per year; i.e., 15 per semester to validate 60 ECTS credits, not counting EIP credits.

Chinese courses represent 2-4 credits.


Academic calendar

The academic year at Feng Chia University lasts 2 semesters:

  • From the beginning of September to mid-January of the following year
  • Winter Vacation: mid January to mid-February
  • From mid-February to mid-June


Department and Courses

The lessons are given in English.

Our students have access to the Master program of Information Engineering and Computer Science (English program), as well as courses in the Department of Information Engineering and Computer Science.



Course format and Workload

Courses are generally theoretical and mathematically oriented.

Important notes 

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial overview (4th year at Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).

Other expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: 700-1000€ depending on the company and dates
  • Visa: about 60€
  • Administration fee: 90€ (student group insurance, internet, student card, airmail fee)
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ depending on the company and coverage
  • Medical examinations: about 20€
  • ARC (within thirty days after your arrival): 30€
  • NHI after living in Taiwan for over 6 months: 20€/month
  • Deposit: usually one or two months, so about 800€ depending on your rent

Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the New Taiwanese Dollar. 1 € = 35.84NTD or TWD (rate October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.


Prices are indicative and may change.

Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • You need to have cash on hand because in Taiwan most payments are made by cash.
  • Make sure to check the withdrawal rights abroad on your credit card before arriving, or use a card such as Revolut (no fees with at Cathay United Bank ATMs).
  • Make sure you pack thick clothes, as it is very humid in Taiwan and can be cold during the winter.
  • It rains a lot in Taiwan, make sure you have an umbrella with you at all times. You can wait until you get there to buy one, they're cheap and get stolen easily!
  • For transport, you have: the HSR (equivalent of TGV in France), the TRA (the local, slower trains), buses (can be less reliable), the MRT, and the bikes.
  • Taiwanese people eat out a lot and you have all sorts of options: night markets, local stalls, breakfast restaurants, buffets, convenience stores, Japanese chains, etc.
  • Scams are quite rare in Taiwan: prices are pretty reliable and it is very safe.
